summary: Richard von Glahn works in sinology and history/archaeology. He served as a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989 and became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987.

Rico Sennrich is a computational linguist. He earned his PhD at the University of Zurich, studying there from 2004 to 2013, before lecturing at the University of Edinburgh (2015–2022) and holding a post at Zurich around 2018.
Rigdzin Shikpo was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under teachers Chögyam Trungpa and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Rigzin Lhundup worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, attested in 1959 and 1987.

Riika J. Virtanen specializes in Tibetology. She pursued doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under doctoral supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.
Rik Pinxten works in philosophy, religious studies, and related fields. He completed his doctoral studies at Ghent University in 1975 and served on its faculty from 1981 to 2012.

Rikizan Ishikawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1962 to 1973. He later served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at Komazawa University from around 1988 until 1997.

Ringu Tulku is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, learning under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Tubten Tsondru.

Rinzin Thargyal worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a Magister degree at the University of Oslo by 1985, supervised by Fredrik Barth and temporary supervisor Arne Martin Klausen.
Rita Gupta is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under David Friedman and held a post at North-Eastern Hill University.

Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg in 2004 under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying at SOAS and other institutions before joining the University of Bristol.

Rita M. Gross was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her degree at the University of Chicago. She held posts at UW-Madison, the American Academy of Religion, and was Professor Emerita at UW–Eau Claire.

Rizong Sras Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who trained at Drepung Loseling Monastery, studying under the 14th Dalai Lama, Losal Ling Khen Zur Jampal Sampel, and Pema Gyaltsen. He served as Abbot of Gyume, Drepung Loseling, and Samstanling, and Ganden Tripa (2009–2016).

Ričardas Mironas was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Vytautas Magnus University and the Sorbonne. He held academic positions at Vytautas Magnus University beginning in 1944 and became a professor at Vilnius University in 1950.

Rob Linrothe specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. After earning his PhD from the University of Chicago, he held posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009), the Rubin Museum of Art (2002–2004), and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

Rob Nairn was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Zimbabwe, King's College London, and the University of Edinburgh. He held faculty posts at the University of Zimbabwe and the University of Cape Town (~1976–1988).

Robert A. F. Thurman is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Geshe Wangyal, Gelek Rimpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama, and held positions at Amherst College (1973–1988) and Columbia University (1988–2019).

Robert A. Hall, Jr. was a linguist educated at Princeton, Sapienza University of Rome, and the University of Chicago under Leonard Bloomfield and Carl Darling Buck. He held positions at Puerto Rico, Princeton, and Brown, and was a Cornell professor (1946–1976).
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin in 2002 under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle.

Robert Alexander Neil was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Aberdeen and Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell and others. He served as a fellow and senior tutor at Pembroke College and Cambridge University Lecturer in Sanskrit (1883–1901).
